question.text: Which of the following correctly distinguishes between company deposits and company debentures?

answer.text: Company deposits are secured while company debentures are unsecured
Both are identically structured with no meaningful difference in security
Company deposits are unsecured with slightly higher returns, while company debentures are normally secured with slightly lower returns
Company debentures are unsecured with higher returns than company deposits

explanation.text: The Logic: Per NISM Series X-B, company deposits are unsecured obligations of the company and carry relatively higher risk with slightly higher returns. Company debentures are normally secured against the company's assets, which lowers the risk to the investor and is accompanied by slightly lower returns. The correct option mirrors this source distinction. The Trap: The first option simply reverses the security status, while the last option transfers the unsecured tag to debentures. Candidates who anchor on the word "deposit" (because of bank deposits) may incorrectly assume company deposits are secured or insured. Note: Any deposit-insurance comparison with bank fixed deposits should be supported by a separate, dedicated source; it is not covered on the checked X-B page for company deposits versus debentures.
